title: Why is Canberra the capital of Australia, not Sydney?

sources.name: National Capital Authority � Canberra, the Seat of Government
National Capital Authority � The Siting and Naming of Canberra

practice: Try World Capitals and see how often the best-known city differs from the capital.

sections.title: Why Canberra, not Sydney or Melbourne?
sections.html:
Canberra is Australia�s capital because the new federation chose a separate home for its national government, rather than favouring Sydney or Melbourne. Rivalry between New South Wales and Victoria helped shape the compromise.

When six colonies united in 1901, the country needed a national capital. As the National Capital Authority explains, the best-known city did not automatically get the job.

sections.title: The rule that kept Sydney out
sections.html:
The Constitution required the capital�s territory to be within New South Wales and at least 100 miles from Sydney, about 160 kilometres. Parliament would meet in Melbourne until the new capital was ready.

That was not a rule to build exactly halfway between the two cities. It was a political compromise, not a geometry puzzle.

sections.title: When did Canberra become the capital?
sections.html:
The answer depends on which stage you mean:

  • 1908: Parliament selected the Yass�Canberra district.
  • 12 March 1913: the city was officially named Canberra.
  • 1927: federal Parliament moved there from Melbourne.

Choosing a site, naming a city and opening its Parliament were separate steps.

sections.title: Was Sydney ever Australia�s national capital?
sections.html:
No: Sydney was not the national capital before Canberra. Melbourne was the temporary home of the federal Parliament.

Canberra was not the only candidate either. More than 60 New South Wales centres were proposed; Dalgety was an earlier parliamentary choice. The National Capital Authority follows the selection.
